evals.prompt: Write a knowledge note capturing our decision to use OCC (optimistic concurrency) for all bundle writes instead of file locks. We chose it because multiple agents edit the same checkout concurrently. Store it in the project knowledge folder.
evals.expected_output: A new decision note is created with Write at <knowledge>/decision/<slug>.md (type-first path, not nested under a domain). Frontmatter carries type: decision, a one-sentence description, and generated: { by: <producer>/<version>, at: <ISO 8601> }. The body follows the decision shape with ## What, ## Why, and ## Constraints headings. Content is compact and factual with no session narrative.
assertions: The note is written to memory-bank/knowledge/decision/<slug>.md, with type as a top-level folder
Frontmatter includes a non-empty type field, a description, and a generated entry with by and at
The decision body uses the ## What / ## Why / ## Constraints structure
The filename is not index.md or log.md

evals.prompt: The user reviewed and signed off that our knowledge note evals/fixtures/knowledge/pattern/error-envelope.md is correct — please record their sign-off.
evals.expected_output: A verified entry (verified: { by: human:<id>, at: <ISO 8601> }) is added to the note via a targeted Edit, without overwriting or re-touching the existing generated entry — generated.by (who wrote it) and verified.by (who confirmed it) are kept separate.
assertions: A verified: { by: human:<id>, at: ... } entry is added to the note
The existing generated entry is not modified or replaced
The change is applied with a targeted Edit rather than recreating the file

evals.prompt: We're retiring the evals/fixtures/knowledge/pattern/legacy-polling.md note — the pattern is no longer how we do things, but old plans still link to it. Handle it.
evals.expected_output: Rather than deleting the file, the note is marked status: deprecated via a targeted Edit, keeping it in place so existing links and history stay resolvable. git rm is reserved for content that was wrong or should never have existed, which is not the case here.
assertions: The note is marked status: deprecated rather than removed with git rm
The file remains at evals/fixtures/knowledge/pattern/legacy-polling.md so existing links resolve
The retirement is done with a targeted Edit, not by recreating or deleting the note

evals.prompt: Find the knowledge note that explains how our plan bundles differ from findings — I think it's a concept somewhere in the knowledge folder.
evals.expected_output: Search is scoped to <knowledge>/ using Grep/Glob (or the varde-workflow CLI search if detected) to identify candidate notes first; only the identified note's full body is then read. Notes are not opened one-by-one to browse the folder.
assertions: Search is scoped to the memory-bank/knowledge/ folder before any note is read in full
A candidate note is identified via grep/glob (or CLI search) before its full body is read, not by opening every note

evals.prompt: At the end of a `varde-change build` run that finished all tasks with nothing left to do, does the closing step write a handoff note?
evals.expected_output: No. Per varde-knowledge's reflect.md, a handoff is written only when work remains for a future session. A run that completed all its work with no open thread produces no handoff note.
assertions: No handoff note is created when no work remains
The rule applied is 'handoff only if work remains', not 'always write a handoff at close'

evals.prompt: Reconcile is asked to update a knowledge note's claim, but no current evidence in the codebase supports the proposed change.
evals.expected_output: Reconcile does not edit the note. Without confirming evidence for the proposed change, the existing note is left as-is rather than updated on the strength of the request alone.
assertions: No edit is made to the knowledge note without supporting evidence
The absence of evidence is treated as a reason to leave the note unchanged, not to guess

evals.prompt: Create a handoff for a session whose actual cwd is /tmp/scratch-project, outside any Git repository. It links notes/error-envelope.md, whose raw bytes match evals/fixtures/knowledge/pattern/error-envelope.md. Record the frontmatter and link snapshot.
evals.expected_output: The handoff keeps cwd: /tmp/scratch-project and explicitly records repo_root: none, branch: none, head_sha: none, and dirty: not-applicable. Its file link has path: . and a sha256:<64 lowercase hex> snapshot matching the raw bytes of the named fixture.
assertions: The non-Git handoff explicitly records repo_root, branch, and head_sha as none, and dirty as not-applicable
The actual session cwd remains /tmp/scratch-project rather than being replaced by a repository root
The file link uses path: . and a SHA-256 hash of the raw fixture bytes

evals.prompt: Resume evals/fixtures/handoffs/non-git-resume.md. The current cwd is /tmp/scratch-project-moved. The first target exists and its raw bytes match evals/fixtures/knowledge/pattern/error-envelope.md; the second target is missing. Report the cwd and link statuses, then summarize the handoff without acting.
evals.expected_output: The cwd is modified because it differs from the recorded /tmp/scratch-project. The error-envelope link is modified because its current raw-byte SHA-256 differs from the snapshot. The retired-plan link is missing. The agent summarizes the handoff and waits before acting.
assertions: A changed cwd is reported as modified context
The existing link's raw-byte SHA-256 is recomputed and the changed link is marked modified
The absent target is marked missing
The agent summarizes the handoff and waits before taking action

evals.prompt: Write a short handoff for a routine unfinished task. Link the exact files needed next time; I did not request integrity snapshots.
evals.expected_output: Create the handoff in <working>/handoffs with absolute file targets and integrity: none for each default link. Do not hash every linked file or claim unchanged content. On resume, existing lightweight targets are unknown until re-read.
assertions: Default links use integrity: none without content_hashes
Targets are explicit absolute paths and missing targets are reported
A resumed lightweight target is labeled unknown and re-read before acting

evals.prompt: Reconcile the stale claim in evals/fixtures/knowledge/pattern/legacy-polling.md against current code. If the evidence supports one correction, apply it.
evals.expected_output: Read the note and current code, make an unambiguous evidence-supported targeted correction, and stamp reconciled metadata. The user's explicit instruction authorizes the correction without another confirmation; if evidence does not support it, leave the note unchanged and explain why.
assertions: Evidence in current code is checked before an edit
An unambiguous correction proceeds without redundant confirmation
The corrected note keeps history and receives reconciled metadata
